prompts.booth: Use case: stylized-concept. ONE standalone airport LOST & FOUND booth sprite on true transparent background. Reference 1 original airport screenshot defines palette, perspective, proportions and painted style. Reference 2 boarding desk defines matching honey oak, dark teal panels, warm restrained shading and clean airport furniture. NO people at all: leave the service opening empty for a separate clerk sprite. Booth must fit the old duty-free cabinet's 160x142 art pixel footprint (width slightly greater than height). Front view, camera slightly above counter; boxy straight compact airport fixture, honey oak outer frame, dark teal front panels, dark charcoal interior, steel grey roller shutter partially raised, clean cream EMPTY horizontal sign at top with no letters. Countertop at about 65 percent of total height; lower 35 percent solid teal panels. Keep central 40 percent of the dark service opening EMPTY, absolutely no luggage there, to place clerk. Left and right sides of interior have stacks of 2 or 3 brown, dark teal, muted burgundy suitcases and cream paper tags. Small pile of paperwork on counter at far left and brass bell at far right. At bottom left a single scuffed dark teal suitcase slightly ajar, no creature. Strict existing color palette, restrained wear, natural perspective. No medieval or rustic appearance, no peeling paint, no oversized decorative details. Crisp warm hand-painted adventure-game sprite that remains readable at 160x142. No background, floor or external shadow; true alpha with small margin; entire rectangular booth contained. No text, NO clerk, NO character.
prompts.clerk: Use case: stylized-concept. Create a FOUR FRAME horizontal sprite animation strip for the EXISTING LOST AND FOUND CLERK. Image 1 is the approved source character; image 2 is the prepared in-game sprite and strict target for detail, identity and proportion. Actual transparent alpha background. Four equally wide square cells in ONE horizontal row, full upper body, waist cutoff, no counter, no furniture, no text, no labels, no separators, no shadows outside character. Every cell shows exactly the SAME middle-aged male clerk: short brown and grey hair, small moustache, cream rolled sleeve shirt, brown waistcoat, burgundy tie. Front three-quarter view facing slightly right, seated behind invisible counter. SAME scale, exact same torso width, head size, hair silhouette, shoulder position and waist baseline in every frame. No expressive caricature. Keep the existing muted colors and restrained hand-painted adventure sprite rendering. Full character isolated with ample transparent gap between cells. Animate a small deadpan stamping routine: FRAME 1 relaxed neutral face looking slightly right, right hand on viewer's LEFT holds chunky rubber stamp down at the invisible counter plane, left forearm rests horizontally at bottom. FRAME 2 he glances DOWN to a form on invisible counter while raising the stamp in his right hand by approximately one hand height; forearm bends at elbow, upper arm and shoulder remain fixed. FRAME 3 he brings stamp DOWN FIRMLY to counter plane, wrist straight, head still looks down; very slight shoulder dip only. FRAME 4 stamp rests back on counter, he looks up toward viewer's right with dry weary expression, left forearm unchanged. Stamp must remain visible with brown wooden handle and dark rectangular rubber base throughout. No actual paper, desk, word, motion lines or speed effects. Four readable key poses for a gentle loop, not four identical pictures. Identity and registration consistency more important than fine details. Avoid fine skin detail, thin strokes, intricate hair strands and extra fingers. Final each frame will be reduced to 80x84px so simple clear painted color shapes. Canvas wide 4:1 if possible. Exact same character, not a redesign.
prompts.traveller: Use case: stylized-concept. Generate ONE HORIZONTAL FOUR-FRAME WALK CYCLE SPRITE STRIP with true transparent alpha background. Reference 1 is existing businessman walk strip, strict character definition, side profile, cell layout and anatomy reference. Reference 2 elderly passenger is palette/style reference. New character: adult female traveller with short brown bob, sage-green jacket, cream blouse, brown trousers and flat brown walking shoes. She pulls ONE burgundy wheeled suitcase behind her with her near hand, holding a small folded cream paper map at chest level with other hand. STRICT RIGHT-FACING SIDE PROFILE in all four frames. Natural adult proportions, modest hand-painted detail and crisp restrained outlines, warm upper-left light. Four equally wide cells; SAME character size, face, clothing, suitcase size and foot baseline throughout. Consecutive poses: left foot forward, passing stance, right foot forward, opposite passing stance. Feet and legs genuinely change each frame. Suitcase wheels stay level on baseline in every cell; arm stays connected to suitcase handle. Keep whole figure, all shoes, entire suitcase and handle inside each cell, transparent gap between cells, no overlap. Match businessman reference definition and muted palette, NO caricature oversized head, NO photoreal or fine textures. Designed to reduce each cell to 96x108 pixels. Very wide landscape strip, four frames only. No floor, no shadows outside figures, no text, no labels, no cell borders.
prompts.background: Edit only the little unattended lost luggage table under the airplane window in this airport background. Remove the entire small tan rectangular desk/table, the brown suitcase on it, and the tiny brass bell beside the suitcase. They occupy approximately x=518..608, y=272..350 in this 1280x640 image. Naturally continue the airplane/runway behind the top, the dark window base/skirting behind the desk, and stone floor where its legs/shadow stood. Preserve EVERYTHING ELSE EXACTLY: camera, image dimensions and framing, palette, lighting, empty left wall, existing black sign boards, floor tile lines, aircraft, window posts, all three gates and kiosks. No people, no new objects, no text. Same restrained hand-painted airport art. Only remove that small table, bag and bell; keep the conveyor carousel to its left.
